prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Time for common sense: trust people, not government. The Conservatives will set families, entrepreneurs, professionals and local institutions free—while nurturing the national traditions and democratic independence that make Britain strong.

Families and schools
- Cut taxes where pressures are greatest: raise the Children’s Tax Credit by £200 for under‑5s; restore a Married Couple’s Allowance worth around £1,000; reform Working Families Tax Credit so it’s paid to the caring parent; scholarships to help parents return to work.
- Back marriage and parental authority; tackle disruption with easier exclusions and new Progress Centres.
- Create Free Schools: heads and governors run schools, reward good teachers, expand successful schools, allow new faith/parent/charitable schools; Parent’s Guarantee to trigger Ofsted and change failing management.

Law and order
- More police, less paperwork; visible policing (“cops in shops”), parish constables; zero tolerance of loutish behavior.
- Tenfold expansion of Secure Training Centres; mandatory jail for dealers selling to under‑16s; tougher sentences for dealing near schools.
- Honest sentencing; real work in prisons; lifetime supervision for serious sex offenders; victims get named contacts and proper explanations.

Earning a living
- A tax‑cutting, deregulating government within a disciplined framework. Save £8bn versus Labour plans and return it in targeted cuts: abolish taxes on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner Personal Allowance by £2,000 (1m off tax); boost family reliefs; cut petrol by at least 6p; abolish IR35; simpler, lower CGT.
- No stealth taxes: transparent national accounts, independent oversight, regulatory budgets that fall yearly.
- Keep the pound; strengthen Bank of England independence; prudent spending within trend growth; scrap the Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear’s role.

Health
- Match NHS spending plans but end political micromanagement. Patient’s Guarantee: maximum waits based on clinical need (starting with cancer and cardiac), and the right to be treated elsewhere—NHS or private—at NHS expense.
- Restore ward authority (Ward Sisters/Matron); GP and patient choice of hospital; expand practice nurses; create high‑throughput surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund; end tax penalties on employer and employee private medical insurance; properly fund hospices.

Older people
- Respect and independence, not means‑testing: abolish most savings taxes; raise the basic state pension with extra for over‑75s; optional consolidation of allowances; end compulsory annuitisation at 75; consult on funded pension options for the young; protect against catastrophic long‑term care costs.

Britain in the world
- In Europe, not run by Europe: keep the pound and veto; renegotiate Nice; reserve powers in UK law; complete the single market and fight fraud.
- NATO first; no EU army; back US missile defence; fully man our forces and curb political correctness.
- Lead on global free trade by 2020; focus aid on good governance, double the share via charities, create “Aid Direct”; tougher, fair asylum: secure reception centres, safe‑country rule, new Removals Agency.

Stronger society, town and country
- Office of Civil Society; cut charity VAT; “Britain Works” pays providers for real jobs; Can Work, Must Work; expect work from lone parents with over‑11s; protect disabled people’s savings; national anti‑fraud squad.
- Foot and Mouth recovery; cut business rates for village shops/pubs/garages/post offices; benefit card to keep post offices viable; abolish top‑down housebuilding targets; protect “Blue Belts”; urban Regeneration Companies; expand homeownership (right‑to‑buy discounts, rent‑to‑mortgage, homesteading); transport investment, 80mph where safe, Brit Disc for foreign lorries.

Culture and democracy
- Free the arts and sport: privatise Channel 4; create a £3bn endowment from its sale and Lottery surpluses; protect school playing fields; single, pro‑competition media regulator and fair BBC oversight.
- Power local people: devolve to high‑performing “free councils”; local referendums on big Council Tax rises; scrap regional quangos; English Votes for English Laws; strengthen an independent, partly elected House of Lords; reduce ministers, MPs and spin doctors.

Time to deliver common sense.
